question: What is the main goal of checking clinical skills before graduation?

options.A: To decide the monthly salary for incoming staff
options.B: To make sure students can safely manage cases on their own
options.C: To replace classroom exams with hospital tests
options.D: To cut down the working hours needed for trainees

explanation: This check ensures trainees have the practical skills needed to practice safely once they graduate. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are practical skills assessments so important in busy maternity units?

options.A: It removes the need for any future training
options.B: High patient numbers mean every student must master procedures to keep care safe
options.C: Patients refuse care without a laminated card
options.D: Government rules require daily written tests

explanation: Busy wards expose students to many cases, making proper skills checks essential for maintaining high standards and patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which procedure is used during antenatal care to check the baby's position and lie?

options.D: Active management of the third stage

explanation: Abdominal palpation using Leopold's maneuvers is the standard clinical method to determine fetal position and presentation during antenatal visits. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h2)

question: You are monitoring a woman two hours after a normal delivery. Which finding needs an immediate response?

options.A: Moderate lochia rubra on the pad
options.B: A soft, relaxed uterus with heavy bleeding
options.C: An axillary temperature of 37.1 degrees Celsius

explanation: A soft or boggy uterus indicates uterine atony, which is the leading cause of primary postpartum hemorrhage and requires prompt action. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main use of a clinical skills passport?

options.A: To track daily financial allowances for interns
options.B: To keep a portable record of practical skills you have completed
options.C: To act as a textbook for advanced lectures
options.D: To replace the hospital duty roster for night shifts

explanation: The skills passport travels with you to document every successfully completed clinical procedure during your ward rotations. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do assessment checklists include infection control along with the final result of a procedure?

options.A: Infection control is the only thing preceptors are allowed to grade
options.B: Hospital management only checks the utility room
options.C: Safety and sterile technique are core parts of good midwifery care
options.D: Patients will not let students touch them without a sterile gown

explanation: A procedure is only done well if it maintains hygiene and prevents infections, making technique just as vital as the final result. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h3)

question: What does DOPS stand for in clinical training?
explanation: DOPS is a common assessment method where a preceptor watches and grades you while you perform a specific clinical task. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of getting feedback right after a DOPS session?

options.A: It guarantees you will never make another clinical error
options.B: It removes the need for written exams
options.C: It lets you correct mistakes and improve your technique right away
options.D: It stops patients from ever complaining

explanation: Immediate feedback connects the observed action with helpful advice while the clinical scenario is still fresh in mind. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is simulation training helpful even when students spend months working in active wards?

options.A: Simulation is only meant for doctors
options.B: Mannequins are cheaper than real patients
options.C: Rare emergencies might not happen during your specific ward rotation
options.D: Ministry rules forbid students from touching real emergencies

explanation: Simulations ensure that every student gets to practice handling critical emergencies, regardless of what happens naturally on the ward. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is a main goal of the discussion session after an emergency simulation?

options.A: To talk about team decisions and find ways to improve care
options.B: To check the physical neatness of the mannequins
options.C: To calculate the cost of medical supplies used
options.D: To give disciplinary warnings for minor mistakes

explanation: This debrief gives the team a chance to reflect on what went well and how communication or technique can be improved during a real crisis. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h5)

question: What does SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Antenatal record, Bed number
options.D: Sterile technique, Birth rate, Assessment, Resuscitation

explanation: SBAR is a structured tool used by health professionals to share concise and critical patient information clearly. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h6)

question: You are handling three patients at once: a woman in early latent labor, a woman with a severe headache and high protein in her urine, and a mother wanting a routine check. Who should you see first?

options.A: All three patients at the same time
options.B: The woman in early latent labor
options.C: The mother wanting a routine check
options.D: The woman with a severe headache and protein in her urine

explanation: A severe headache and proteinuria point strongly toward pre-eclampsia, a serious emergency that needs immediate attention. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h6)

question: How should clinical preceptors view a skill a student struggles with during an assessment?

options.A: As an administrative error to ignore
options.B: As a reason to end the internship immediately
options.C: As proof that the student is unsuited for healthcare
options.D: As a chance to provide extra support and targeted practice

explanation: Assessments help catch weak spots so they can be fixed through extra practice before graduation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard support plan for a student needing extra help?

options.A: Extra supervised practice hours on the ward
options.C: Clear timelines for a future re-assessment
options.D: Immediate expulsion from the training institution

explanation: Support plans are designed to help students improve through teaching and extra practice, not to punish them with expulsion. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h7)

question: Who usually sits on the final review panel for graduating midwifery students?

options.A: Incoming first-year students and junior aides
options.C: Senior ward managers, clinical coordinators, and nursing tutors

explanation: A panel of clinical and academic leaders reviews all records to ensure every graduation requirement has been met. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h8)

question: What main responsibility starts as soon as you begin independent practice?

options.A: Working without ever looking at hospital guidelines
options.C: Taking full professional responsibility and knowing when to ask for senior help
options.D: Taking over management of the whole maternity department

explanation: Independent practice means you are legally responsible for your actions and must know your limits to call for senior assistance when needed. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h8)
